name: Retro Arcade
tagline: Build a Power BI report on a pre-made arcade-themed semantic model, level by level.
description: Insert the coin. You get a Direct Lake semantic model packed with decades of 80s arcade high-scores (Pac-Man, Galaga, Donkey Kong & friends). Your job: build a Power BI report that climbs 5 levels — Foundation, Visuals, Interactivity, Storytelling, Polish. The Check notebook reads your PBIR definition with sempy, grades each level, and mints a signed badge from Newbie all the way to Kill Screen Survivor.
learning_objectives: Connect a Power BI report to a published Direct Lake semantic model
Use a variety of visual types (cards, slicers, matrix, charts)
Configure sync slicers, edit-interactions, and cross-page filters
Add bookmarks, tooltip pages, and drill-through pages
Apply custom themes, conditional formatting and mobile layouts
Inspect a report's PBIR definition programmatically with sempy

items.name: Arcade_LH
items.description: Holds synthetic arcade Delta tables: Scores (~80k), Games (12), Players (40), Cabinets (8), Date (3 years).

items.name: 01_Setup
items.description: Run once: generates seed data, builds ArcadeHall_Model Direct Lake semantic model with relationships and base measures.

items.name: 02_Quest
items.description: The 5 levels brief. Read this before building the report.

items.name: 03_Check
items.description: Reads your Arcade_Hall_Report via sempy, grades each level (20 pts max), assigns rank, mints signed badge.
